name.ja: ジェレミー・ベンサム

overview.en: Jeremy Bentham was an English philosopher and jurist who founded utilitarianism, the ethical theory that actions should maximize the greatest happiness for the greatest number.

early_life.en: Born in London to a wealthy family, he was a child prodigy who attended Oxford at age twelve and trained as a lawyer but never practiced.

impact.en: His utilitarian philosophy reshaped law, economics, and public policy, and his ideas on individual liberty, animal rights, and prison reform were centuries ahead of their time.

event.en: Published A Fragment on Government, critiquing Blackstone
Published An Introduction to the Principles of Morals and Legislation
Designed the Panopticon, an innovative prison concept

title.en: An Introduction to the Principles of Morals and Legislation

text.en: The greatest happiness of the greatest number is the foundation of morals and legislation.

quotes.source: An Introduction to the Principles of Morals and Legislation

text.en: The question is not, Can they reason?, nor Can they talk?, but, Can they suffer?
